extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics faculty, department chairs, and assessment coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for departments to design and conduct formative and summative assessment of teaching and programs in undergraduate mathematics, including techniques, departmental supports, evaluator roles, and interpretation of student ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Program Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Program evaluation is to judge the worth of a program and, in education, requires that assessment of student learning take place. Program evaluation may also include implementation problems, costs of the program, and communication with interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of student learning is a means to achieve program evaluation and also to understand how students learn and to evaluate individual students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Student Learning (distinct from program evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of student learning is a means of understanding how students learn and of evaluating individual student performance; it is not identical to program evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessment data to inform program evaluation, but recognize different purposes and contexts for each activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Mixed Methods (qualitative + quantitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine qualitative and quantitative methods in evaluation (e.g., interviews, observations, tests) because they can corroborate and illuminate one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: interview data raised concerns about computational skills; subsequent quantitative tests corroborated those concerns; follow-up interviews helped interpret attitude instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative vs Summative Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Formative evaluation provides ongoing feedback during a course (the cook tastes the soup); summative evaluation assesses outcomes after completion (the guests taste the soup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is not always a clear distinction: summative findings can be used to inform course changes and thus become formative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inside vs Outside Evaluator Roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside evaluators know the program well but are subject to bias; outside evaluators are less familiar but can serve as consultants and auditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both: insider conducts most evaluation; outsider periodically inspects and certifies that the evaluation is fair and accurate (acts like a CPA/auditor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Prepared for Unexpected Results and Seek Alternative Explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: When conducting evaluation, expect and plan for results that are unexpected or unfavorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always look for sources of bias and alternative explanations; be clear and honest about limitations without being paralyzed by them; beware administrators who request evaluations for bureaucratic reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Uniform, Replicable Grading Schemes and Use Multiple Graders
rubrics_metrics.description: Create grading schemes that are uniform and replicable across graders and courses and, where possible, employ multiple graders to improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reduce bias and improve comparability of assessment results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have an Outside Reviewer for Plans and Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Get an outsider to review evaluation plans and results to guard against bias and to certify fairness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside reviewers serve as consultants and auditors and can improve credibility of the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Expectations for Teaching Improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The department should create and communicate a strong expectation that members will improve teaching (via policy decisions, hiring criteria, exemplary practice, daily conversations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A departmental climate of expectation supports junior faculty and fosters sustained improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Departmental Resources for Teaching Improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should provide time- and money-based resources: senior mentoring, shared materials (network drives), information on conferences/workshops, support for publishing scholarship on teaching, course development grants, and retreats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many supports involve time rather than money; retreats can be inexpensive and effective for sharing innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage Campus Centers for Teaching and Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use institutional centers for teaching and learning for diagnosis, consultation, videotaping/debriefing, resource libraries, publicity, and teaching institutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers provide expertise and services (e.g., videotaping, monthly interdisciplinary discussions) that amplify departmental efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Retreats and Assessment Workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Run retreats/workshops to set individual and departmental teaching goals, use inventories (e.g., Teaching Goals Inventory), and learn specific formative assessment techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior reading and inventories can prepare faculty; workshops model the value of assessment and help set concrete goals for using techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Portfolios as an Assessment and Documentation Tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Course portfolios document materials prepared for a course (notes, exercises, projects, labs), include representative student work, and may contain a reflective teaching journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portfolios can be used for subsequent evaluation and to support scholarship on teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midcourse (Formative) Evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect feedback from students midsemester to provide timely information about teaching effectiveness and student learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Midcourse evaluations allow instructors to adjust while the course is in progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Muddiest Point" and Similar Quick-Formative Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short formative techniques such as asking students to identify the muddiest point to diagnose and address confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widely used and easy to implement for quick feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly Self-Evaluated Take-Home Quizzes (with e-mail reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give weekly take-home quizzes with solutions on the back; require students to self-report performance by e-mail and ask questions; record participation but do not grade the quizzes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages reflection, low-stakes practice, and creates a channel for students to ask about difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Concept Maps for Pre-Unit Assessment and Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement concept maps to assess students' prior knowledge and to facilitate review of key relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reveal students' conceptual organization and misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Journals for Reflective Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Have students keep journals about their course experiences to surface attitudes, difficulties, and learning progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals give insight into student thinking and changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail Servers / Class Journals for Out-of-Class Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Create e-mail forums or class journals to extend discussion outside class and to solicit structured responses to prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an asynchronous forum for questions and can serve as a class-level journal of ideas and misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Evaluation Model (multiple components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a multi-component professional evaluation model designed to foster mathematical maturity while ensuring mastery of fundamental skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines several assessment methods to balance skill mastery and higher-level learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Prompts to Probe Conceptual Understanding (e.g., 'What is abstraction?')
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign short essays asking students to articulate concepts (such as abstraction) to gauge changes in their perspectives as they progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for assessing maturation in mathematical thinking beyond procedural ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Observation and Colleague Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer faculty pairs observe each other, review course materials and student work, and meet regularly to discuss teaching and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides targeted formative feedback and is an extension of team-teaching culture; valuable for both junior and senior faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of Student Evaluation Instruments (item content and framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey items should align with contemporary definitions of effective teaching rather than assuming an 'authority/presenter' model; items often elicit subjective responses (e.g., 'prepared for class', 'relates well to students', 'grading').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully construct items to reflect desired instructional outcomes and avoid biased framings that reward poor practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and Weighting of Student Evaluation Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Common practices include computing a composite score by weighted averaging (example: an 'overall' item weighted half and remaining items combined weighted half).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about weighting; recognize limitations of reducing complex data to a single number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and Misuse of Student Evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Student evaluations can be inconsistent with other measures of teaching effectiveness, may be gamed (faculty can improve ratings by doing things not considered pedagogically sound), and are better described as 'opinions' than as full 'evaluations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat student evaluation scores as the preponderance of evidence; use them as one input among many.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Mandates vs Local Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: External mandates (e.g., Regents requiring use of student evaluations) may prescribe that student data be collected but do not mandate that such data be the dominant evidence of teaching effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments should interpret mandates in ways that incorporate multiple measures and align with local standards of effective teaching.
